utterances.speaker: David Whitfield
utterances.text: Morning, everyone. Friday the 23rd of October. Can you hear me, or am I talking to the little spinning wheel again?

utterances.speaker: Fiona Doyle
utterances.text: We can hear you. Important opening observation: there's a birthday cake in the office.

utterances.speaker: Tomasz Nowak
utterances.text: That's my weekend plans sorted, then. Was going walking, but have you seen the weather? Rain sideways.

utterances.speaker: Marcus Hale
utterances.text: So you're walking as far as the cake. Sensible risk assessment.

utterances.speaker: Tomasz Nowak
utterances.text: Warmer there than this portakabin. The heating in here is either tropical or absolutely nothing. Just moaning, not asking for a job on it.

utterances.speaker: David Whitfield
utterances.text: Right, before this becomes the cake and heating meeting. Finished bits first, then what actually needs doing.

utterances.speaker: David Whitfield
utterances.text: I already swapped the filter on the fire panel yesterday. That's finished, not another filter job for today.

utterances.speaker: Aisha Begum
utterances.text: Yeah, and I tested the IM3 yesterday and it's all fine now. Nothing outstanding from that test.

utterances.speaker: Sarah Okafor
utterances.text: I signed off the inspection on the fire alarm panel on Tuesday as well. That one's closed.

utterances.speaker: Olumide Adeyemi
utterances.text: Lovely. Three things we don't need to go round again.

utterances.speaker: Sarah Okafor
utterances.text: Less lovely, we're still waiting on parts for the line 3 chiller. Nothing we can do until they arrive.

utterances.speaker: Sarah Okafor
utterances.text: And same story on the 11kV board, still waiting on parts. Nothing we can do until they arrive either.

utterances.speaker: Fiona Doyle
utterances.text: Both still blocked, then. Not fresh actions for anyone this morning.

utterances.speaker: David Whitfield
utterances.text: Correct. Also, I noticed the palletiser was running a bit warm on nights, but it settled down. That's just an observation, not another job.

utterances.speaker: Aisha Begum
utterances.text: Right, settled down. Keep that separate from anything we're actually agreeing.

utterances.speaker: David Whitfield
utterances.text: Marcus, can you check the guarding on the Palletiser this afternoon? That one's safety critical, straight away.

utterances.speaker: Marcus Hale
utterances.text: Yeah, I'll check the guarding on the Palletiser this afternoon. Straight away when we get into that afternoon work, safety-critical one first.

utterances.speaker: David Whitfield
utterances.text: Exactly. Not bundled in with that low-level warm-running observation.

utterances.speaker: David Whitfield
utterances.text: Tomasz Nowak, can you swap the filter on the dryer today? It's urgent.

utterances.speaker: Tomasz Nowak
utterances.text: Yep, I'll swap the filter on the dryer today. Understood, urgent.

utterances.speaker: Olumide Adeyemi
utterances.text: Sorry, you clipped there—different filter from the fire panel one you just mentioned?

utterances.speaker: David Whitfield
utterances.text: Yeah, completely separate. Fire panel was yesterday and done. The dryer is the live job.

utterances.speaker: David Whitfield
utterances.text: And I'll write up the near miss at the Boiler Safety Relief Valve this morning. That one's safety critical, straight away.

utterances.speaker: Sarah Okafor
utterances.text: Thanks, Dave. The near-miss write-up is with you this morning, then.

utterances.speaker: David Whitfield
utterances.text: Yes, mine. Definitely not leaving that floating between us.

utterances.speaker: Marcus Hale
utterances.text: While we're on the team stuff, I'll organise the toolbox talk for the team next week.

utterances.speaker: Fiona Doyle
utterances.text: Cheers, Marc. Next week for organising the toolbox talk, yeah?

utterances.speaker: Marcus Hale
utterances.text: Yeah, next week. I'll take that.

utterances.speaker: Sarah Okafor
utterances.text: I'll sort the training records for the new starters by the 28th. That's a whenever you get a chance one, rather than drop everything, but still by the 28th.

utterances.speaker: Fiona Doyle
utterances.text: Got you, Saz. Training records with you, by the 28th, around the higher-priority stuff.

utterances.speaker: Sarah Okafor
utterances.text: Exactly. It's mine, just not a stop-the-world job.

utterances.speaker: Olumide Adeyemi
utterances.text: Um, the sensors on the line 1 mould temp need recalibrating first thing tomorrow. The priority wording on that is whenever you get a chance. I haven't got an owner for it.

utterances.speaker: Aisha Begum
utterances.text: Sorry, first thing tomorrow, despite the whenever-you-get-a-chance bit?

utterances.speaker: Olumide Adeyemi
utterances.text: Yeah. Recalibrate the sensors on the line 1 mould temp, first thing tomorrow. That's the requested timing; it hasn't been marked urgent.

utterances.speaker: David Whitfield
utterances.text: Right. Does anyone here actually have that, rather than us assuming somebody does?

utterances.speaker: Tomasz Nowak
utterances.text: Not me. I can't take that one on.

utterances.speaker: Olumide Adeyemi
utterances.text: And I'm raising it, not volunteering for it. Don't put my name against it just because I mentioned sensors.

utterances.speaker: David Whitfield
utterances.text: Fair point. Agreed it needs doing first thing tomorrow, but the recalibration is unassigned.

utterances.speaker: Fiona Doyle
utterances.text: Another gap: someone needs to schedule downtime for the palletiser with production after lunch. Low priority. That's not allocated either.

utterances.speaker: Sarah Okafor
utterances.text: Low priority for the scheduling, yes. Not saying the guarding check is low priority—before those get mixed up.

utterances.speaker: Fiona Doyle
utterances.text: Exactly. After lunch is when the scheduling needs doing, not me declaring a downtime slot after lunch.

utterances.speaker: David Whitfield
utterances.text: Understood. Anyone taking the production scheduling bit?

utterances.speaker: Sarah Okafor
utterances.text: I can't take it. Please don't assume shift management means it's automatically mine.

utterances.speaker: Fiona Doyle
utterances.text: Nor am I accepting it here. I'm flagging the gap.

utterances.speaker: David Whitfield
utterances.text: Okay. Scheduling downtime for the palletiser with production, after lunch, low priority, still no owner.

utterances.speaker: David Whitfield
utterances.text: I will take the other conveyor one, though. I'll clear the jam and check the sensors on the outfeed conveyor by Thursday.

utterances.speaker: Olumide Adeyemi
utterances.text: Davey, that's both clearing the jam and checking the sensors, by Thursday?

utterances.speaker: David Whitfield
utterances.text: Yep, both with me, by Thursday.

utterances.speaker: Aisha Begum
utterances.text: Right, outfeed conveyor. Separate entry from the palletiser discussion.

utterances.speaker: David Whitfield
utterances.text: Yeah. Too many things ending in conveyor and panel this morning.

utterances.speaker: Marcus Hale
utterances.text: One more, and this isn't a casual one. We need someone to take vibration readings on the GT2 by 11am. Drop everything for that one. Nobody's taken it.

utterances.speaker: Fiona Doyle
utterances.text: By 11am, highest urgency, but no name. That's a fairly big hole.

utterances.speaker: David Whitfield
utterances.text: It is. Can anyone actually accept the GT2 readings?

utterances.speaker: Marcus Hale
utterances.text: I can't commit to it. I know I'm the one saying it, but I'm not taking ownership.

utterances.speaker: Olumide Adeyemi
utterances.text: I can't take it either. Sorry—talked over you there.

utterances.speaker: David Whitfield
utterances.text: No, you're all right. The GT2 vibration readings remain unowned. By 11am, drop everything for that one; the urgency hasn't gone away because there's no taker.

utterances.speaker: Fiona Doyle
utterances.text: So the three gaps are the line 1 mould temp recalibration, the palletiser downtime scheduling, and the GT2 vibration readings. None accepted.

utterances.speaker: David Whitfield
utterances.text: That's right. Quick check on the things people have actually accepted, then we'll finish.

utterances.speaker: Tomasz Nowak
utterances.text: The dryer filter is mine today, urgent. No confusion with yesterday's fire panel filter now.

utterances.speaker: Marcus Hale
utterances.text: I've got the Palletiser guarding this afternoon, safety critical, straight away. And organising the toolbox talk for the team next week.

utterances.speaker: Sarah Okafor
utterances.text: Training records for the new starters with me by the 28th, whenever I get a chance. The two parts-blocked items stay blocked.

utterances.speaker: David Whitfield
utterances.text: And mine are the Boiler Safety Relief Valve near-miss write-up this morning, safety critical, straight away; then the outfeed conveyor jam and sensor check by Thursday.

utterances.speaker: Aisha Begum
utterances.text: Nothing else from me. IM3 was the completed update, not something to carry forward.

utterances.speaker: Fiona Doyle
utterances.text: Good. And the cake was information only. Although it may not survive this meeting.

utterances.speaker: David Whitfield
utterances.text: Probably the clearest status we've had all morning. Thanks, everyone. We'll leave it there.
